scope: Where the expert formal model (formal/) departs from the source documents. Only the formal model and the documents are compared; results/, claims/ and flow/ are not part of this file. Entries marked material=false were found in passing; the minor list is not exhaustive.

categories.contradiction: The formal model does something the documents rule out.
categories.convention: The formal model fixes a choice the documents leave open or do not state.
categories.scope: The formal model contains content that is not in the documents.

doc_check.confirmed: The quoted text was checked in the document, or the document was searched and is silent on the point.
doc_check.pending: Not yet confirmed against the whole document set.

formal.excerpt: out(att,(idB_2, (Nb_2, senc(((idA_2, (Na_2, Tb_2))), Kbs_2)))); ... out(att,(cypher2_2, Ma_2)); ... out(att,(cypher6_2, Mb_2));

entries.description: The cleartext components of messages (2), (1') and (2') are in a different order from the message notation, which follows the original publication and SPORE: (2) carries N_b before the encrypted instructions, (1') the ticket before N_a', (2') {N_a'}K_ab before N_b'. The order of (2) and (1') matches the Wikipedia description the upstream AutoSM model was written from; the order of (2') has no source. The ciphertext contents, on which the Hwang type-flaw attack depends, are the same.
entries.verification: Re-running the model with the three messages in the notation's order gives the same result on all six queries.

formal.excerpt: (new Kas_2:bitstring; ... (Alice(Kas_2, id(Kas_2), id(Kbs_2)))) ... (Server(Kas_2, Kbs_2, id(Kas_2), id(Kbs_2))))))))

document.quote: the key registered for principal B with the KDC

entries.description: The KDC does not look up keys by identity: each replicated instance creates one pair of long-term keys and runs A, B and the KDC for that pair, with the keys passed as parameters. The document has the KDC use the key registered for the requesting principal.
entries.verification: Not material: a lookup by identity admits every session the per-pair instances admit and more, so the false verdicts remain; and the document requires no check that the model omits.

formal.excerpt: let ((=idB_2, (=Na_2, (Kab_2:bitstring, Tb_2:bitstring))))=mess1_2 in ... in(att,(=idA_2, Na_2:bitstring)); ... let ((=idA_2, (Na_2:bitstring, Tb_2:bitstring)))=mess3_2 in

document.quote: verifies that the nonce N_a is the same as that included in message (1)

entries.description: The model adds identity checks the document does not state: A checks B inside message (3), B checks the claimed A in message (1), and the KDC checks both names. The document only has A check N_a in message (3).
entries.verification: Re-running the model without A's check of B in message (3) gives the same result on all six queries. Removing checks only admits more runs, so the other added checks cannot carry a false verdict either.

document.quote: for repeated mutual authentication requiring only four messages initially and three messages for subsequent

entries.description: Subsequent authentication runs once, directly after the initial exchange in the same session, and B accepts only the same ticket ciphertext it received there. The document lets A use the ticket for later, repeated authentications, with B checking that the ticket has not expired.
entries.verification: Not material: repeated use of any valid ticket admits every run the model admits and more, so the false verdicts stand; the model's same-ticket requirement is stricter than the document, not looser.
